answer: Each agent identity can be required to post a bond that is locked before it may submit work, and slashed if later evidence shows coordinated fraud, such as many identities reusing the same payment source and producing matching claims. Honest agents recover their bonds, but an attacker must tie up real capital for every fake identity and risks losing it; making a Sybil swarm large enough to sway outcomes becomes costly. A copper ledger, cedar audit trail, and ocean of fabricated accounts do not remove that financial exposure.
